docs.title: Linux Command Reference
docs.text:
A quick reference guide for common Linux commands used throughout the training course.

This document is designed as a companion reference and does not replace the individual lessons.

docs.title: pwd - Print Working Directory
docs.text:
Shows your current location.

pwd

Example:

/home/james/projects

docs.title: ls - List Files
docs.text:
Displays files and directories.

Basic usage:

ls

Detailed listing:

ls -l

Show hidden files:

ls -a

Human-readable sizes:

ls -lh

Common combination:

ls -lah

docs.title: cd - Change Directory
docs.text:
Move between directories.

Go to home directory:

cd

Go to a specific directory:

cd /etc

Move up one level:

cd ..

Return to previous directory:

cd -

docs.title: mkdir - Create Directory
docs.text:
Create a directory:

mkdir directory-name

Create nested directories:

mkdir -p projects/linux/module01

docs.title: touch - Create Empty File
docs.text:
Create a file:

touch notes.txt

Create multiple files:

touch file1.txt file2.txt

docs.title: cp - Copy Files
docs.text:
Copy a file:

cp source.txt destination.txt

Copy directories:

cp -r directory backup-directory

docs.title: mv - Move or Rename
docs.text:
Move a file:

mv file.txt /tmp/

Rename a file:

mv oldname.txt newname.txt

docs.title: rm - Remove Files
docs.text:
Remove a file:

rm file.txt

Remove a directory:

rm -r directory

Force removal:

rm -rf directory

⚠️ Use rm -rf carefully.

docs.title: rmdir - Remove Empty Directory
docs.text: rmdir directory-name

docs.title: cat
docs.text:
Display file contents:

cat filename

docs.title: less
docs.text:
View large files page by page:

less logfile.txt

Useful keys:

q       Quit
space   Next page
/word   Search

docs.title: head
docs.text:
Display first lines:

head file.txt

Specify number of lines:

head -n 20 file.txt

docs.title: tail
docs.text:
Display last lines:

tail logfile.txt

Follow live changes:

tail -f logfile.log

Commonly used for log monitoring.

docs.title: find
docs.text:
Search the filesystem.

Find by name:

find /home -name "*.txt"

Find files:

find . -type f

Find directories:

find . -type d

docs.title: locate
docs.text:
Fast file searching.

locate filename

Update database:

sudo updatedb

docs.title: grep
docs.text:
Search inside files.

Example:

grep error logfile.txt

Recursive search:

grep -r "error" /var/log

docs.title: chmod
docs.text:
Change permissions.

Make a script executable:

chmod +x script.sh

Numeric permissions:

chmod 755 script.sh

docs.title: chown
docs.text:
Change ownership.

Example:

sudo chown james file.txt

Change owner and group:

sudo chown james:developers file.txt

docs.title: whoami
docs.text:
Show current user:

whoami

docs.title: who
docs.text:
Show logged-in users:

who

docs.title: id
docs.text:
Show user information:

id

docs.title: useradd
docs.text:
Create user:

sudo useradd username

docs.title: passwd
docs.text:
Set password:

sudo passwd username

docs.title: groupadd
docs.text:
Create group:

sudo groupadd developers

docs.title: ps
docs.text:
Display processes:

ps

Detailed view:

ps aux

docs.title: top
docs.text:
Live process monitoring:

top

docs.title: systemctl
docs.text:
Manage services.

Check service:

systemctl status ssh

Start service:

sudo systemctl start service-name

Enable at boot:

sudo systemctl enable service-name

docs.title: journalctl
docs.text:
View system logs.

View logs:

journalctl

Follow live logs:

journalctl -f

View service logs:

journalctl -u ssh

docs.title: ip
docs.text:
View network information:

ip addr

View routes:

ip route

docs.title: ping
docs.text:
Test connectivity:

ping google.com

docs.title: curl
docs.text:
Test HTTP services:

curl https://example.com

docs.title: ssh
docs.text:
Remote login:

ssh username@server

docs.title: ss
docs.text:
View network connections:

ss -tulpn

docs.title: df
docs.text:
Display filesystem usage:

df -h

docs.title: du
docs.text:
Display directory usage:

du -sh directory

docs.title: lsblk
docs.text:
Display disks:

lsblk

docs.title: mount
docs.text:
Display mounted filesystems:

mount

docs.title: Debian / Ubuntu
docs.text:
Update packages:

sudo apt update

Install software:

sudo apt install package-name

Remove software:

sudo apt remove package-name

docs.title: Red Hat / Rocky Linux
docs.text:
Install software:

sudo dnf install package-name

Update system:

sudo dnf update

docs.title: echo
docs.text:
Display text:

echo "Hello Linux"

Display variables:

echo $PATH

docs.title: history
docs.text:
Show previous commands:

history

docs.title: which
docs.text:
Locate commands:

which ls

docs.title: man
docs.text:
Display manual pages:

man command

Example:

man ls

docs.title: uname
docs.text:
Kernel information:

uname -r

Full information:

uname -a

docs.title: hostname
docs.text:
Display hostname:

hostname

docs.title: free
docs.text:
Memory usage:

free -h

docs.title: uptime
docs.text:
System uptime:

uptime
